basics.name: Junwoo Jung
basics.label: Physics Undergraduate
basics.summary: Undergraduate researcher in neutral-atom quantum computing and analog quantum optimization, working at the theory–experiment interface of Rydberg-array processors. Primary work develops an approximation-ratio-resolved shots-to-solution framework with an excitation-matched random baseline, isolating genuine quantum structural exploitation from excitation-density effects in MIS optimization. Additional experience in deterministic error mitigation for Rydberg MIS and in quantum resource theories.

courses: Scientific Computing for Quantum Information Science (Graduate)

thesis.title: Combinatorial Optimization on Neutral Atom Arrays: Problem Encoding, Noise Mitigation, and Approximate-Solution Performance Evaluation

work.name: Quantum Computing Lab (Prof. Jaewook Ahn), KAIST
highlights: Developed an approximation-ratio-resolved shots-to-solution (STS) framework for hybrid neutral-atom optimization, modeling postprocessed outputs via a degeneracy-weighted Boltzmann shell distribution parameterized by a single quality parameter β̃.

Introduced an excitation-matched random baseline β̃_rand(p_exc) to isolate genuine quantum structural exploitation from excitation-density effects, correcting a systematic confound in existing Rydberg benchmarking literature.

Ran QuEra Aquila experiments (King's-lattice MIS, N ∈ [30, 125], 500 shots/instance) and measured Δβ̃_ann = 0.23–0.40 across all system sizes and hardness bins, confirming that adiabatic annealing genuinely exploits low-energy solution structure.
Characterized the two-regime STS scaling: exponential in N for near-exact targets (r → 1), O(1) for relaxed targets, establishing the approximation-ratio dependence of the quantum advantage.

Built a deterministic error-mitigation (DEM) pipeline for Rydberg MIS using a binomial Hamming-shell noise model and entropy-controlled classical baselines (2^{N H₂(p)} scaling); analyzed Pasqal Fresnel datasets and extracted instance-dependent success scaling.

work.name: Condensed Matter Theory Group (Prof. Gil Young Cho), KAIST
highlights: Studied the behavior of the chiral central charge beyond strict entanglement-scaling laws, focusing on the structure and interpretation of subleading corrections.

work.name: The inQlings (Prof. Nelly Ng), NTU Singapore
highlights: Investigated the gap between Thermal Operations (TO) and Gibbs-Preserving Covariant (GPC) channels in quantum resource theory.
Produced an internal manuscript draft on catalysis-based approaches relating TO and GPC under robustness assumptions; conjectured that fully non-degenerate spectra make GPC equivalent to TO.

work.name: Quantum Computing Lab (Prof. Jaewook Ahn), KAIST
highlights: Worked on Rydberg-atom graph constructions for QUBO problems on neutral-atom arrays; optimized atom arrangements and graph embeddings supporting the Advanced Quantum Technologies (2024) publication.
Intensive program on New States of Quantum Matter and AI-driven physics.
Completed intensive graduate-level coursework on Scientific Methods for Quantum Information Science (5 ECTS).

Project: implemented classical shadow tomography to detect the 1D transverse-field Ising phase transition, benchmarking shadow-estimated Rényi-2 entropy against exact diagonalization at g/J = 1. View code
